kind: Resiliency
metadata:
  name: {{ .name }}-redelivery
spec:
  policies:
    retries:
      redelivery:
        policy: exponential
        maxInterval: {{ .redeliveryMaxInterval }}
        maxRetries: {{ .redeliveryMaxRetries }}
{{- $appId := .appId }}
{{- $pubsubs := dict }}
{{- if (eq (lower (replace "-" "" .kind)) "transactionalintegration") }}
{{- /* The internal hop's pub/sub, minted by the topology as internal-<component>

{{- $_ := set $pubsubs (printf "internal-%s" .name) true }}
{{- else }}
{{- range .topology.topics }}
{{- if has $appId (dig "subscribers" (list) .) }}
{{- $_ := set $pubsubs .pubsub true }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
  targets:
{{- if $pubsubs }}
    components:
{{- range $name, $_ := $pubsubs }}
      {{ $name }}:
        inbound:
          retry: redelivery
{{- end }}
{{- else }}
    # The topology gives this block no subscription: nothing to retry.
    components: {}
{{- end }}

  - {{ .appId }}

The system-level half of manifest generation: the Dapr components a system's
blocks resolve by name.

Rendered once per system into `domains/<domain>/<system>/host/`.

## Why these objects live here

A Dapr `Component` is namespace-scoped, and every integration in the
cluster's integration namespace shares it. So exactly one ArgoCD Application may own each one. If each
block owned a copy, N Applications would claim the same `Component/pubsub` and
whichever synced last would win — a live example of that exists in one customer
repository today.

This directory is that single owner. `scopes:` is what limits *use*: it lists
exactly the app-ids the topology says publish to or subscribe from the broker.
Single ownership plus scopes is the correct pair; scopes alone is not.

Its `component.yaml` declares `kind: shared`, which is how `intropy deploy` and
`intropy deploy promote` know to refuse it — there is no image to pin.

I've made the template changes on `release/2.0` in intropy-templates; nothing is committed. A local render of the three-integration system, using the edited templates and the topology the new library produces, is now consistent and passes `kubectl apply --dry-run=client`:

- **One Component, `tx-flow-pubsub`,** scoped to `order-sync`, `price-sync` and `stock-sync`.
- **Three Subscriptions** on `tx-flow-pubsub`, with topics `internal-order-sync`, `internal-price-sync` and `internal-stock-sync`.
- **Three Resiliency policies**, each targeting `tx-flow-pubsub`.
- **`INTROPY_SYSTEM_NAME: tx-flow`** on all three CronJobs.

That render used a temporary test in the CLI, which I've deleted.

**What changed:**
- **deploy-host:**
  - `pubsubName` is no longer a parameter (it defaulted to `pubsub`). It's now a derived value, `<system>-pubsub`.
  - The three broker templates only list the scopes of that pubsub.
  - Updated the README, and removed `pubsubName` from the two examples.
  - Credentials were already per system (`<system>-secrets`).
- **deploy-component:**
  - CronJob and Deployment set `INTROPY_SYSTEM_NAME`.
  - The Resiliency template takes a transactional integration's pubsub from its topology subscription, instead of assuming `internal-<name>`.
- **system-host:**
  - The `pubsub` value is now `<name>-pubsub`, so the Taskfile's `dapr publish` and AGENTS.md use it too.
  - Updated the description and the `Messages.cs` comment.
- **extractor** (as you said, assuming the new framework):
  - Removed `Constants.PubSubName`. The publisher gets `Composition.PubSubName(sp)`, which reads `FrameworkOptions.SystemPubSubName` and fails clearly when it isn't set.
  - The integration tests set a system name in code.
  - Updated the docs.
- **loader:** updated AGENTS.md, and the test sidecar's pubsub name.
- **transactional:** AGENTS.md, both READMEs and the composition comment now describe `internal-<app-id>` on the system's pubsub. The author README had been out of date, describing the topic as `<app-id>-in`.
- **CLAUDE.md:** the message-wiring rule now says `<system>-pubsub/<message>`, and that component templates never hard-code a pubsub name.

**One CLI change for the templates:** `internal/template/real_manifest_e2e_test.go` required the extractor's `Constants.cs` to contain `PubSubName = "pubsub"`. It now checks that no pubsub name is hard-coded.

**Testing:**
- I mirrored the uncommitted edits into a throwaway repo in the scratchpad, because the e2e tests clone the committed branch.
- Against that copy, all CLI `e2e` suites pass (deploy, template, system, cmd), and the CLI unit tests pass.
- Five `integration`-tagged deploy tests fail. They fail the same way on the unmodified `release/2.0`, because their fixture topologies have no `subscribes[].resource`. They were already broken before my changes.

**Still open:**
- **Namespace overlay.** `deploy-host/skeleton/overlays/{{ .env }}/kustomization.yaml.tmpl` still hard-codes `namespace: integration`, with a comment saying it's shared by every system and environment. You said there's one namespace per environment, but I don't know the naming convention. Is it the environment name itself, or something like `integration-<env>`?
- **Framework version pins** in the component csproj templates are still `1.2.1-beta.2`. The extractor template won't compile until they're bumped to the release with `SystemPubSubName`. I haven't compiled the scaffolded C# against the local framework.
- **`.entire/`** is untracked in the templates repo. I didn't create it.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - The user started by investigating how the pubsub name is set in `intropy manifests render`. That led to finding that a system made only of transactional integrations (TIs) renders non-deployable manifests.
   - Through discussion we agreed on this design (option 3):
     - Each system owns one Dapr pubsub Component named `<system>-pubsub`, with its own scopes and credentials, pointing at the environment's shared broker.
     - Kubernetes has one namespace per environment, with a RabbitMQ vhost or Service Bus namespace per environment.
     - A TI's internal queue rides the system pubsub on its own topic, `internal-<component>`.
     - The framework derives the pubsub name from `INTROPY_SYSTEM_NAME`, which deploy manifests and the Aspire host set. The environment variable wins over code; setting it in code is only an escape hatch for tests.
   - The user asked me to implement this in framework, topology, CLI and templates. The latest request is "Can you go ahead with the template changes?" (intropy-templates, branch `release/2.0`).
   - Mid-turn the user added: "You can infer the framework changes. They will be released at the same time as the template."

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Dapr scoping:** Components and app IDs are namespace-scoped. Component `scopes` limit which apps may use a Component; `publishingScopes` and `subscriptionScopes` limit topics.
   - **Broker naming:** the Dapr RabbitMQ component names the exchange after the topic (fanout) and each queue `{consumerID}-{topic}`. The Component name never appears on the broker, so a shared topic name causes cross-talk between integrations.
   - **Topology:** the C# topology DSL (`MessageRef<T>.Define`, `InternalQueue`, `TopologyMaterializer`). The graph verb is run by the CLI (`dotnet run -- graph --development`). Aspire runs local F5.
   - **CLI flow:** `manifests render --env local` builds the host and reads the topology. `buildPubSubs` and `manifestSeeds` produce `pubsubName` only when the system has exactly one pubsub. `seedDeclaredParams` keeps only seeds the template declares as parameters.
   - **Templates:** Go `text/template` plus sprig. `spec.values` holds derived values. `spec.files` uses first-match `when` rules.
   - **Framework:** `FrameworkOptions`, `TransactionalIntegrationOptions`, and the `PostConfigure` precedence that lets the environment win.

3. Files and Code Sections:

   **intropy-framework** (branch `fix/queue-subscribe-race-condition`, uncommitted; 861 tests passing)
   - `src/Intropy.Framework.Core/Configuration/Constants.cs`: added `SystemNameEnvironmentVariable = "INTROPY_SYSTEM_NAME"`.
   - `FrameworkOptions.cs`: added `public string? SystemName {get;set;}` and `public string? SystemPubSubName => string.IsNullOrEmpty(SystemName) ? null : $"{SystemName}-pubsub";`, with doc comments saying the environment wins and setting it in code is an escape hatch.
   - `ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs` (Core): reads the environment variable and, when it is set, calls `services.PostConfigure<FrameworkOptions>(opts => opts.SystemName = systemName)`, so the environment wins.
   - `TransactionalIntegrationOptions.cs`:
     - Removed the pubsub constant.
     - Added `internal static string InternalQueueTopicName(string componentName) => $"internal-{componentName.Replace('.', '-')}";`.
     - `UseInternalQueueDefaults(FrameworkOptions framework)` sets the pubsub to `framework.SystemPubSubName`, and throws an `InvalidOperationException` mentioning SystemName, `INTROPY_SYSTEM_NAME` and DaprPubSubName when it is null. The topic is `InternalQueueTopicName(framework.ComponentName)`.
     - Added `using Intropy.Framework.Core.Configuration;`.
   - `TransactionalIntegrationServiceCollectionExtensions.cs`: now calls `options.UseInternalQueueDefaults(sp.GetRequiredService<FrameworkOptions>())`.
   - **Tests:**
     - TI tests set `options.SystemName = "order-flow"` and expect `order-flow-pubsub` and `internal-orders-integration`.
     - Dapr test constants: `SystemName = "test-system"`, `PubSubName = $"{SystemName}-pubsub"`, `Topic = $"internal-{AppId}"`.
     - `SendSideRunTests` and `DaprTopicEnqueuerTests` swap their pubsub and topic names to match.
     - New tests: an error when neither the pubsub nor the system name is set; no system name needed when the pubsub is set; Core tests for env var wins over code, code value as fallback, and unset.

   - `Refs.cs`:

The EndToEnd snapshot's InternalQueue was updated.
